summary:
STS Agniveer is a satellite-based fire monitoring and data harmonization platform that aims to make active fire observations more consistent, accessible and meaningful. Our current prototype focuses on India and uses NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) API and resources to collect observations from two satellite instruments, MODIS and VIIRS.

Since both instruments independently detect fire hotspots, their observations may overlap or represent repeated detections of the same fire event. Our system uses spatial and temporal analysis, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) information and historical observations to identify potential overlaps and reduce duplicate records, making cross-sensor comparisons more meaningful.

The platform provides an interactive hotspot map, area-specific fire activity timelines, historical comparisons and anomaly identification. By transforming scattered satellite observations into an interpretable view of burning activity, STS Agniveer aims to support researchers, forest departments, land managers and citizens with accessible information for better awareness and monitoring. It builds on existing satellite resources, with future scope for validation and wider geographical coverage.
details:
Project Overview

STS.Agniveer is an autonomous Thermal Anomaly Harmonization Engine designed to solve a critical blind spot in Earth observation: satellite data duplication. When monitoring active fires, instruments like MODIS and VIIRS frequently pass over the same region, creating overlapping data points. Our project turns these fragmented, long-running satellite hotspot observations into a single, consistent view of burning activity over time.

How It Works & Technical Stack

Instead of just plotting raw telemetry on a map, our system processes data from NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS) using a custom Python backend.

Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN): We utilize Python and density-based spatial clustering to analyze coordinates. If multiple sensor readings occur within a highly condensed radius, the engine identifies the overlap and merges them into a single harmonized fire event.

Peak FRP Extraction: Rather than averaging data—which could understate a fire's threat—the engine extracts the Peak Fire Radiative Power (FRP) from the cluster to ensure first responders prepare for the maximum observed intensity.

Deployment: The harmonization engine and interactive 3D dashboard are hosted on Vercel, with version control managed via GitHub.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Without harmonization, historical fire patterns and unusual periods can be difficult to interpret consistently. Our tool provides responders and land-management agencies with an area-specific burning-activity calendar.

The primary benefit is distinguishing between expected seasonal burning (like agricultural fires) and critical anomalies. By establishing a localized historical baseline, emergency management teams can confidently allocate resources to high-risk areas without the threat of deploying to "false alarm" density spikes caused by satellite double-counting.

How Our Project is Creative

While many dashboards focus purely on real-time snapshots, STS.Agniveer is creative in its temporal approach. We treat data gaps (such as dense smoke clouds obscuring sensors) not as failures, but as signal degradation signatures that actually indicate a massive fire event. Our design philosophy prioritizes visual storytelling, enabling users to easily compare current anomalies against historical baselines on an interactive globe.

Live Prototype: [https://sts-agniveer-harmonization.vercel.app/](https://sts-agniveer-harmonization.vercel.app/)
